steps.text: She'd considered the possibility of ending it all, even if it meant the fires of the Draco would never die.
She'd imagined the flames of wrath bursting from her aching chest, burning away the shell and identity she had been given, liberating her from the shackles of her self.
But when she truly went to touch her flames, desiring to hold them, she suddenly wondered if she never had control over them in the first place.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You've done well, Loughshinny.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You wanted me to give you my sincere praise. Is this good enough?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Or have you prepared yourself by now... for the shadow to return to the self, for you to replace me as 'The Leader'?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I can give you this opportunity. Your next plume of flames will burn me to ashes.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Will you... reach out to me?
The flames burn, and her shadow sways slightly.
But Reed averts her eyes.
Not far away, Caireann, who has just woken up, slowly props herself up atop an old apron, and Moran hums as she helps clean her wound.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Sister, why did you come back?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: What do you see, as you stand here?
The campfire burned bright that night.
At the time, Fionn was wandering around begging for a new foothold to get business up and running, and Selmon was wrapping more wire around her weapon.
Everyone called her the Leader jokingly, but they were serious when they thanked her for bringing them all here.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I heard that King Gaeil was crowned by the Victorians, and only then did they erect the royal palace over a ceremonial stone circle.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Before that... it was first home to the Tarans.
She thinks back to festive winter nights from long, long ago.
They would change into new, matching outfits in front of the fireplace, leaving behind a photograph of their smiling faces.
What a lovely... warm little ball of flame.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: So... no.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I don't care about being a shadow.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But I am not your shadow. I am simply—the shadow of our people's ideal 'Leader.'

spans.text: shadow. I am simply—the shadow of our people's ideal 'Leader.'

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: They want a way out, a way to get their lives back; I happened to be there, and became needed by them.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: So why must I defeat you, Sister?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Not afraid of death? Please don't say that, Caireann. There's nothing wrong with being afraid of dying.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: How tragic would it be to die at Dublinn's hands before we save our fellow Tarans? Dublinn wants to save them too, you know.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: You're... a lot more well-spoken than before.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Lucky we've still got plenty of anti-inflammatories...

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Ufff...

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Did that hurt? Sorry...

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Ah, Reed, you're back.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: If we hide here tonight, we shouldn't run into any of the Arts-controlled corpses again.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Have you surveyed around us already? That's good.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I wish we could stop a bit longer myself, but Caireann's injuries... aren't looking good.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Hey, what's that look on you for...

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Haha. I still remember at the beginning, we all saw you like you were our doctor. Only later we realized you're just like all of us—wounded.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Are my own wounds, well, er, serious?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No, they aren't... Don't worry. Your injuries can be healed.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's just... are you afraid of my fire?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Of course not.
And so she reaches out, to the wounded Taran in front of her.
The Draco's burning anger wells within her blood. In bygone times, the Red Dragon bled for his people, one drop of his blood incinerating plains from end to end.
She swallows her roiling breath. The suppressed flames scorch her.
But if doing so can soothe pain, then she is willing to endure it.
—It is no true flame that burns in her hands, not even a flash of light.
But invariably, the people are filled with the same feeling—the flowing of life, as gentle as one's eyes opening for the first time to the rays of morning.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I'm guessing by your face... you're already feeling a lot better?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Yeah... Reed, you... maybe you really are a doctor? Still, not that you work the same way other docs do.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No. What these are... are my own flames, at long last.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: May you sleep soundly tonight, Caireann.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Never thought I'd see the day someone outside the Victorian Army would board a high-speed battleship.

steps.name: Dublinn Officer
steps.text: That should've been the first thing on your mind the moment you lowered the Victorian flag.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I have nothing against you, Taran—I just want to see your forces' military proficiency. Plus, I'm rather curious about that Leader of yours.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I certainly hope the Duke's guest isn't just relying on her Draco bloodline.

steps.name: Dublinn Officer
steps.text: Your arrogance towards us seeps from your very bones, Victorian.

steps.name: Dublinn Officer
steps.text: But when she gets up on stage to give her speech, you'll find that she is the true master of the forces on this ship.

steps.name: Wounded Taran
steps.text: I still don't get it. Are you people Dublinn or not? After all, you don't dress anything like them.

steps.name: Wounded Taran
steps.text: But, regardless of who you are, you saved us from the Victorians. I'll follow you anywhere.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...I'm sorry we couldn't—help your friend.

steps.name: Wounded Taran
steps.text: It's fine... it's fine. As long as others can be saved, I suppose you can say he's still living through them.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Alright.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: By the way, Reed, have those people given up on hunting us?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Hmm... The team that was tailing us vanished fairly abruptly, but in any case, things work to our advantage.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Dublinn's forces should be assembled now.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...The Tarans are about to make their voice heard throughout Victoria.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Soldiers.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The Dublinn forces I am in charge of have come from all over Victoria to join His Lordship's army, and together, they will fire the opening shots to the war for their survival.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Up until the last few days, many people may not have heard of the Dublinn name, or have any idea what we are fighting for.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Your war is picking up steam as we speak, but ours has been raging on and on over the last decade. As we speak, those flying the Taran banner continue to bleed.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: There are no words that can describe the atrocities that the Tarans have had to endure. I have seen their streets burned to ash, their cities reduced to rubble.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: And yet they, who deserve everything the land can give them, met with our soldiers at risk of being executed to break their bread with us.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I saw the Tarans crying out to us in their struggles. However, their salvation has been deferred not decades, but entire centuries.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: They appeal to their great and mighty compatriots... and to their neighbors of conscience, to all those Victorians who will not be co-conspirators to tyranny.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: They cry out for our attentive eyes.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: As I speak, there are those among us who are well-aware of their Taran blood. Yet, there are others who may be asking—who exactly are we going to help?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Tarans. Tarans... With all the time we've spent together, we've all gotten used to using this word.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: But what you said never left my mind, Reed. You said the factory workshop we were in lacked protective measures, so everyone would slowly come down with Oripathy and waste away.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Yet, the owner of the factory who drove the Tarans to work under such dangerous conditions... was himself a Taran.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: And there are so many people like you who speak bog-standard Victorian. Though they were born in the same place as us, they're afraid of talking with us, and revealing their accents...

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: What exactly is a Taran? Who is it we're trying to save?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's been on my mind for a long time, too. Do you want to hear what I think?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Go on, Reed. We're not looking forward that badly to fleeing for our lives. Of course we're happy to hear you out.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Mm... At this point, I might say—it's the name given to the centuries of our plight.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: In the past, Victorians spent many years trying to erase the Taran name. But I'm sure you can all feel it—those ties are still there.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Victorians don't call us Tarans. They call us 'nasty-sounding, uncultured bumpkins, good-for-nothing rascals, ill-bred scum'...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Or, as many people have experienced, they strip us of our property, our land, and our rights... even the lives of our kin. All because of our common name.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Some may say to us—then why not give up your language and your traditions? Why not sing the same songs as Victorians at the festivals?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: As long as others can't tell that we're Tarans, we'll be able to receive the same treatment as them.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Of course, there are others who may retort that even though they are Tarans, they've earned wealth through willpower and dedication, receiving enough education to climb up into the upper class.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: —To this I say, how ironic it is that we must throw aside our culture and betray our own name, just to earn the dignity of being seen as ordinary people by them.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Though some of us have achieved greatness, the first step to success invariably is to become Victorian.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Duke Wellington, surely you understand this better than anyone else...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: How many people still remember that your heart pumps a Taran's blood?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But. Given that Victoria is deliberately trying to strip us of our name, does that mean they've really forgotten about Tara's existence?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: If that were the case, then why did I, a descendent of King Gaeil, a surviving Draco, two hundred years after the fall of the Taran kingdom—

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: —Watch my parents be murdered by the Aslans' assassins, left to lie in their own blood?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: No. They are afraid that we will remember our names and expose their lies.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: And I stand before you to remind you of this fact.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: So what you're saying is, years and years ago, the Victorian nobles came to Tara to subjugate all its people?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Yes. That much is what the history books tell us.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There's numerous fabrications about Tara, but some interspersed truths too.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Victoria forcibly put King Gaeil into power as monarch of the Tara region, coercing him to canonize many Victorian nobles. The unfair treatment towards Tara as a land was codified into law, too.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Since then, the Taran's accent has been associated with their lowly status. The Victorians have come to see the Tarans as stupid, vulgar, and uneducated.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But who will come to educate the people of Tara? In all these hundreds of years, not a single soul.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The Tarans have slowly fled from their homeland, perhaps drifting through Victoria along with its nomadic cities, but never enjoying the same rights and privileges as the Victorians.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Have we ever had seats at prestigious banquets or institutions of higher education? If there are layabouts among us, is that not because the Victorians have taken away our right to work?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The injustices we've long endured were so cleverly hidden away in the lengthy years after the word 'Taran' was expunged. But, no longer. We finally understand why we have been driven to despair.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There is much I know, both about Tara's history, as well as about the legends spun by subsequent generations to trace Tara's origins.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I can tell you about everything—true injustices, and fabricated dreams alike.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But I won't speak of them. You'll all want to... escape from your past lives.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Well, of course! We can't live on like this!

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Mm. So, it's alright even if we can't tell we're Tarans.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I just think—wherever the lights-out chimes, everyone must need a flame that burns through the night.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: The only thing we must fight is the misfortune thrust upon us.

a.text: Therefore, to fight for the Tarans' survival is something we must do.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Right now, we are docked in Oak Grove, once a Taran community burned to ashes by a tyrant's flames.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Perhaps those with keen enough eyesight will be able to see Tara's palace destroyed by a Catastrophe over yonder. Such are the scars left behind on the Taran people.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: However, it is hardly our intent to recover Tara's ancient lands, or reconstruct our history out of its tatters.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: We are wanderers in a new land, and the road I wish to take you down is one of constructing a new era and a new order.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: —This battleship's next stop will be at the port of Londinium.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Naturally, we are not going to compete for Victoria's crown. We simply are taking our destiny back from the Victorians, into our own hands.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Our eyes are open now—we clearly see that our suffering is rooted in the dominion and servitude that Victoria imposed upon Tara. As such, we ought to let Victoria deny the legitimacy of its own past actions.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The war may not end in Londinium, but surely we do not fear a long and bitter fight?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The flames have already been kindled.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: They will burn away the ancient order of this land, taking our rotten shackles along with it.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: As for the new order that shall be established, I turn to all of you.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I implore all of you, regardless of whether you're Taran or Victorian, regardless of who you are or where you came from, to simply fight for the glory of justice, for the unprecedented era to come.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Until the Tarans are free to compose their own dreams, just as the Victorians are, nothing shall stand in our way.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: But, Reed, what are we fighting for? 'For the survival of the Tarans' is simply too vague.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Mm... In past times, I always thought—that life was so fragile.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Upon this great land, many a thing waits to take our lives from us. Everything we do is no more—than a desperate struggle, a stand, against death.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: And in the end, one from which nobody can emerge victorious.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: If I concerned myself too much with people's lives, how would I ever be able to come face-to-face—with the all too ubiquitous sacrifices, with the sea of unmarked graves?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Yet—the weight of a life... is immense. That is something I can't escape from.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: We cannot defeat death. But we can—and we should—give dignity to the living.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I believe... that the people of Tara should have a warm fire at night, and wine in their glasses when they sing their songs.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There should be a day, when the people of Tara no longer have to run away, or bid farewell to their families and lovers.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I hope—for the people of Tara to have their own homeland, where they can live in peace.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I hope... that all those we've parted ways with—will all be reunited there.
The wind rustles the reeds, and amidst their swishing, she feels the painful sear of the dancing flames.
She sees that it is an austere, yet distant dream. Perhaps, not a single person standing here will be here to see that day come.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Dublinn's flames will burn this land.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Surely... it will be harrowing. Thousands upon thousands of lives, nothing more than fuel for the flames of war.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But even then, the weight of a life cannot ever be diminished.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Let's go. We are a part of it too.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Oh, right, I got a letter from home yesterday.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: They're all alive and well. Maybe when we get back from war, they'll be doing even better. Haha!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Lost for words again, Moran?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Sorry. I couldn't help wondering to myself. What should living life be like?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Well, how about starting with a song?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Go on. You might as well—nobody's after our heads for once.
By the firelight of homely hearth I sleep, dreaming of honey, rum, and stew ♪

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Say, Reed. What are you gonna do if we end up siding with Dublinn?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Don't worry.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There's no difference between her and I. We're both trying to realize the same single dream for the Taran people.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: When that day comes, I will go see her.
